I have resolved the issue where `Model.objects.all().delete()` was generating a subquery `DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM table)`.

### Root Cause
In `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`, the calculation `sum(self.query.alias_refcount[t] > 0 for t in self.query.alias_map) == 1` was evaluated without ensuring the base table alias had been added to `self.query.alias_map`. For `Model.objects.all()`, `alias_map` was empty (`{}`), causing `single_alias` to evaluate to `False` and fall back to subquery generation.

### Solution
- Called `self.query.get_initial_alias()` inside [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-wqia275t/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1412) to ensure the base table alias is registered prior to checking alias reference counts.
- Added a test [`test_fast_delete_all`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-wqia275t/tests/delete/tests.py#L641-L647) to verify that `QuerySet.all().delete()` generates `DELETE FROM table` directly without subqueries.
